analysis: The PR changes only the LifecycleTests.setUp fixture in .github/scripts/test-threat-budget.py (head lines 927-931). It pins GITHUB_RUN_ATTEMPT="1" in the test env dict so a runner-inherited attempt value of "2" does not turn every scan into a MANUAL_SCAN_RERUN_DISABLED rerun. This is a test-only fixture with no production code path, no provider, coordinator or attestation behavior, no keys, no cache storage, and no endpoints. None of the threat-model entries are touched (A-001..A-019, TB-002..TB-013, T-041 and the rest are unrelated to this CI test harness). The only security-adjacent consideration is that the existing test test_manual_github_rerun_hands_off_without_any_paid_work still overrides the attempt to "2" via env.update (base line 951), so the rerun-disabled guard retains test coverage. Pinning the attempt to "1" cannot weaken the production rerun guard, because the production code reads the real environment, not this dict. No regression, new attack surface or threat-model gap was identified. The review covered the patch and the base text excerpts, including the unchanged surrounding tests. I did not review the production budget_runner, which is outside the supplied evidence, but the change does not depend on it.
